newsitem.title: NICARAGUA: Volcano alert issued in Nicaragua.
newsitem.headline: Volcano alert issued in Nicaragua.

text.p: Nicaraguan officials issued an alert on Friday after a volcano near the capital started rumbling, periodically spewing gases and ash.

"The Santiago Volcano has increased its volcanic activity and is periodically emitting ashes and gases, as well as making rumbling sounds," a Nicaraguan Institute of Territorial Studies (Ineter) news release said.
Ineter warned that activity at the Santiago Volcano, 12 miles (20 kms) southeast of Managua, could cause tremors and further emissions of ash.

Authorities have closed the surrounding Masaya National Volcanic Park to visitors as a precaution. The park is a popular tourist spot where visitors can drive right to the edge of Santiago's crater and see a small pool of lava below.
Santiago Volcano has rumbled on and off for much of the 1990s but has not had a major emission of lava, Ineter said.
